te.sit:aisha-sibaq:0: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ on one of his journeys when I was a young girl and had not put on weight. He said to the people: “Go on ahead,” and they went ahead. Then he said to me: “Come, let me race you.” So I raced him and I beat him, and he said nothing. Later, when I had put on weight and had forgotten, I went out with him on another journey. He said to the people: “Go on ahead,” and they went ahead. Then he said: “Come, let me race you.” I raced him and he beat me, and he began to laugh, saying: “This is for that.”
te.sit:ghart-ummukum:0: The Prophet ﷺ was with one of his wives when one of the Mothers of the Believers sent a dish of food. The wife in whose house the Prophet ﷺ was struck the servant's hand, and the dish fell and broke. The Prophet ﷺ gathered the broken pieces of the dish, then began collecting on them the food that had been in it, saying: “Your mother became jealous.” Then he kept the servant until a dish was brought from the wife in whose house he was, and he gave the sound dish to the wife whose dish had been broken, and kept the broken one in the house of the one who broke it.
te.sit:muawiya-hakam:0: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished praying — may my father and mother be his ransom — I never saw a teacher before him or after him who taught better than he did. By Allah, he did not scold me, strike me or revile me. He said: “Nothing of people's talk is fitting in this prayer; it is only glorification, declaring Allah's greatness, and recitation of the Quran.”
te.sit:shab-zina:0: A young man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, give me permission to commit zina.” The people turned to him and rebuked him, saying: “Stop! Stop!” He said: “Come close.” He came close and sat down. He said: “Would you like it for your mother?” He said: “No, by Allah, may Allah make me your ransom.” He said: “Nor do people like it for their mothers…” Then he placed his hand on him and said: “O Allah, forgive his sin, purify his heart and guard his chastity.” After that the young man never inclined towards anything of the kind.
te.sit:farah-tawba:0: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than one of you who was on his mount in a waterless desert, and it ran away from him carrying his food and drink. He lost hope of it, went to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of his mount. While he was in that state, there it was, standing before him. He took hold of its reins and said out of extreme joy: “O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord” — he erred out of extreme joy.
te.sit:qatil-mia:0: …He asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth and was directed to a scholar. He said: “He has killed a hundred people; is there any repentance for him?” He said: “Yes; who stands between him and repentance? Go to such and such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah; worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is an evil land…”
te.sit:abubakr-umar-khilaf:0: There was a dispute between Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, and Abu Bakr angered ‘Umar, so ‘Umar left him angrily. Abu Bakr followed him, asking him to seek forgiveness for him, but he would not, and shut his door in his face… The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah sent me to you and you said: ‘You are lying,’ while Abu Bakr said: ‘He has spoken the truth,’ and he supported me with himself and his wealth. Will you then leave my companion alone for me?” (twice)
te.sit:sam-alaykum:0: A group of Jews came in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “As-samu ‘alaykum” (death be upon you). ‘A'ishah said: I understood it and said: “And upon you be death and the curse.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Gently, O ‘A'ishah! Allah loves gentleness in all matters.” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I already said: ‘And upon you.’”
te.sit:abuhurayra-juu:0: Summary of the report: Abu Hurayrah used to tie a stone over his stomach out of hunger. The Prophet ﷺ passed by him, smiled when he saw him, and knew what was in his heart. He took him to his house, where he found a bowl of milk, and told him to invite the people of al-Suffah. He gave them all to drink, then gave him to drink until he was full, and then the Prophet ﷺ drank what was left.
te.sit:umm-sulaym:0: Summary of the report: A son of Abu Talhah died while he was away. When he returned he asked about him, and Umm Sulaym said: “He is calmer than he has ever been.” Then she prepared supper for him, and afterwards told him through a parable: “If some people lent a household something and then asked for it back, would they refuse them?” He said: “No.” She said: “Then seek reward for your son.” He told the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “May Allah bless the two of you in your night.”
te.sit:jabir-dayn:0: Summary of the report: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram died owing a debt. (Jabir said:) I asked the Prophet ﷺ to help me with his creditors so that they would reduce some of his debt. The Prophet ﷺ asked them but they refused. He said to me: “Go and sort your dates into their kinds…” Then he came and sat at the top — or in the middle — of them, and said: “Measure out for the people.” I measured for them until I had paid them all that was due to them, and my dates remained as if nothing had been taken from them.
te.sit:jurayj:0: Summary of the report: Jurayj's mother called him while he was praying, and he said: “O Lord, my mother and my prayer!” and carried on with his prayer. She prayed against him, and he was tested with a woman's accusation against him. The people demolished his hermitage. He prayed, then asked the baby: “Who is your father?” It said: “The shepherd.” And Allah cleared him.
te.sit:ashab-ghar:0: Summary of the report: A rock rolled down and blocked the cave on them. They said: “Nothing will save you except to call upon Allah by your righteous deeds.” The first sought Allah's help by his devotion to his parents; the second by his abstaining from indecency out of fear of Allah; and the third by having grown his labourer's wages and returned them to him in full. And the rock moved away.
te.sit:salman-abuddarda:0: Salman said to him: “Your Lord has a right over you, your soul has a right over you, and your family has a right over you; so give each one who has a right their due.” Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about it, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Salman has spoken the truth.”
te.sit:hanzala:0: …By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you remained in the state you are in when you are with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and in your streets. But, O Hanzalah, there is a time for this and a time for that (three times).
te.sit:abudhar-jahiliyya:0: O Abu Dharr, did you taunt him about his mother? You are a man who still has some traits of the days of ignorance. Your servants are your brothers whom Allah has placed under your authority. So whoever has his brother under his authority, let him feed him from what he eats and clothe him from what he wears, and do not burden them with what is beyond them; and if you do burden them, then help them.
te.sit:mughith-barira:0: The Prophet ﷺ said to ‘Abbas: “O ‘Abbas, are you not amazed at Mughith's love for Barirah and Barirah's dislike of Mughith?” Then the Prophet ﷺ said (to Barirah): “Why not go back to him?” She said: “O Messenger of Allah, are you ordering me?” He said: “I am only interceding.” She said: “I have no need of him.”
te.sit:fatima-khadim:0: Shall I not teach you both something better than what you asked me for? When you go to bed, say “Allahu akbar” thirty-four times, “Subhan Allah” thirty-three times and “Al-hamdu lillah” thirty-three times; that is better for you both than a servant.
te.sit:iqilha-tawakkul:0: A man said: “O Messenger of Allah! Shall I tie it (my camel) and rely upon Allah, or leave it loose and rely upon Allah?” He said: “Tie it and rely upon Allah.”
te.sit:iqilha-tawakkul:1: If you were to rely upon Allah as He should be relied upon, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full.
te.sit:hatab-karama:0: It is better for any of you to take a rope, bring a bundle of firewood on his back and sell it, so that Allah saves his face because of it, than to ask people, whether they give him or refuse him.
te.sit:hatab-karama:1: No one has ever eaten food better than what he eats from the work of his own hands; and the Prophet of Allah Dawud, peace be upon him, used to eat from the work of his own hands.
te.sit:jar-mataa:0: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining about his neighbour. He said: “Go and be patient.” He came to him two or three times, and then he said: “Go and throw your belongings out into the road.” So he threw his belongings into the road, and people began asking him and he told them what had happened, and people began cursing the neighbour… Then his neighbour came to him and said: “Go back; you will not see anything from me that you dislike.”
te.sit:saad-wasiyya:0: A third, and a third is a lot. It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor, begging from people. You will not spend anything seeking the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it, even what you put in your wife's mouth.
te.sit:qabil-habil:0: Do not envy one another, do not inflate prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another… and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.
te.sit:qarun:0: Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling Allah's favours upon you.
te.sit:sulayman-naml:0: How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good, and this is for no one except the believer: if something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him; and if something bad happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.
te.sit:yusuf-muraawada:0: Seven people Allah will shade with His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His… and a man who is called by a woman of status and beauty and says: “I fear Allah.”
te.sit:luqman-wasaya:0: All of you are shepherds and each of you is responsible for his flock… A man is a shepherd over his family and is responsible for his flock, and a woman is a shepherd in her husband's house and is responsible for her flock.
te.sit:adam-iblis:0: Every son of Adam sins, and the best of those who sin are those who repent.
te.sit:zakariya-dua:0: The supplication of any of you is answered as long as he is not hasty and says: “I supplicated but I was not answered.”
te.sit:musa-khidr:0: Musa the Prophet stood up to address the Children of Israel and was asked: “Who is the most knowledgeable of people?” He said: “I am the most knowledgeable.” Allah admonished him because he did not attribute knowledge to Him, and Allah revealed to him: “A servant of Mine at the junction of the two seas is more knowledgeable than you.”
te.sit:abasa:0: “He frowned and turned away” was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, the blind man. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “O Messenger of Allah, guide me,” while one of the leading men of the idolaters was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
te.sit:hajar-zamzam:0: “O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person and nothing?”… Then she said to him: “Is it Allah who has commanded you to do this?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “Then He will not let us be lost.”… The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is the running of the people between them (Safa and Marwah).”
te.sit:himar-khamr:0: Do not curse him, for by Allah, I know nothing of him except that he loves Allah and His Messenger.
te.sit:himar-khamr:1: Do not be helpers of Satan against your brother.
te.sit:sadaqa-sariq:0: A man said: “I will certainly give some charity.” He went out with his charity and put it in the hand of a thief… Then it was said to him: “As for your charity to a thief, perhaps it will make him refrain from his stealing; as for the adulteress, perhaps it will make her refrain from her adultery; and as for the rich man, perhaps he will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him.”
te.sit:wahshi:0: When he saw me, he said: “Are you Wahshi?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Are you the one who killed Hamzah?” I said: “What happened is as you have heard.” He said: “Can you keep your face away from me?” So I went out.
te.sit:waswasa-sarih:0: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came and asked him: “We find in ourselves thoughts that each of us considers too grave to utter.” He said: “Do you really find that?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “That is clear faith.”
te.sit:waswasa-sarih:1: Praise be to Allah who has reduced his (Satan's) scheming to mere whispering.
te.sit:waswasa-sarih:2: Satan comes to one of you and says: “Who created this? Who created that?” until he says: “Who created your Lord?” When it reaches that, let him seek refuge with Allah and stop.
te.sit:safiyya-ghiba:0: You have said a word which, if it were mixed with the water of the sea, would change it.
te.sit:safiyya-ghiba:1: “Do you know what backbiting is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “It is your mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes.”
te.sit:fatima-qays:0: As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his stick down from his shoulder; and as for Mu‘awiyah, he is poor and has no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd. I disliked him, but he said again: “Marry Usamah.” So I married him, and Allah put good in him, and I came to be envied.
te.sit:thabit-khul:0: “O Messenger of Allah, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays for his character or his religion, but I dislike ingratitude (to my husband) in Islam.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Will you give him back his garden?” She said: “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said (to Thabit): “Accept the garden and divorce her once.”
te.sit:sahl-ayn:0: Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something in his brother that he likes, let him pray for blessing for him.
te.sit:hummara:0: Who has distressed this bird by taking her young? Give her young back to her.
te.sit:hummara:1: Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal which Allah has given you possession of? It has complained to me that you keep it hungry and overwork it.
te.sit:ibn-abbas-ihfadh:0: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation gathered together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with what Allah had already written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with what Allah had already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.
te.sit:liqa-allah:0: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; and whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him. ‘A'ishah said: “But we dislike death.” He said: “It is not that. Rather, when death comes to the believer, he is given glad tidings of Allah's pleasure and honour, so nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead of him.”
te.sit:abusufyan-heraclius:0: By Allah, had I not been ashamed that they would report me as having lied, I would have lied about him… Heraclius said: “I asked you whether you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said, and you said no. So I know that he would not refrain from lying about people and then lie about Allah.”
te.sit:mumin-qawi:0: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: “If only I had done such and such, it would have been so and so,” but say: “Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does,” for “if only” opens the door to the work of Satan.
te.sit:mumin-qawi:1: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men.
te.sit:hubb-fillah:0: A man visited a brother of his in another town, and Allah placed an angel on his road to watch for him… The angel said: “Do you have any favour from him that you are seeking to increase?” He said: “No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” The angel said: “I am a messenger from Allah to you, to tell you that Allah loves you as you have loved him for His sake.”
